automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Leaf Update Watch

cutoff_window.qualification_rule: Only sources with direct visible publication or update dates from 2026-09-01T01:02:58Z through 2026-09-08T01:02:58Z qualify; relative-only, missing, ambiguous, future-dated, and boundary-only dates are excluded.

federation_boundary.local_owner_scope: AI-assisted development lens: context architecture, guidance structure, agent operating practices, workflows, verification, governance, and local adoption patterns.
federation_boundary.routing_note: Broad ecosystem entity details are upstream-owned; this artifact records only downstream local-practice implications.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub Copilot weekly releases say Copilot app and CLI now honor content exclusions, Copilot for JetBrains has a generally available harness, VS Code adds Agent Merge, experimental multi-root workspaces for Copilot and Claude sessions, and hierarchical chat sessions that show attention state.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Selected workspace, handoff, coordination, readiness, recovery, and governance leaves depend on whether agent sessions expose workspace boundaries, attention state, merge-readiness work, and sensitive-code exclusion evidence.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Review persistent workspace and cross-environment handoff leaves for session hierarchy, multi-root workspace, content exclusion, and Agent Merge evidence.

qualifying_updates.visible_date: released this 03 Sep 01:37; 04 Sep 23:25 hotfix also visible
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: OpenAI Codex release notes for 0.153.0 list plugin CLI marketplace operations, complete TUI history for patches, background-terminal input, and completed commands, session reconnect after app-server drops with uncertain queued submissions paused, Guardian review history surviving compaction/restarts/forks, account-scoped remembered MCP approvals, rollout compression/resume handling, and later hotfixes for Astra visibility and async-question guidance.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Runtime updater integrity and recovery leaves need versioned receipts for updater behavior, approval history, compressed session replay, MCP approval scoping, and plugin marketplace operations before local setup guidance changes.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Review updater, lifecycle-hook, session-recovery, MCP-approval, and plugin-packaging leaves for Codex 0.153 runtime receipts.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub Copilot code review now includes approval assessments and can be admin-authorized to approve pull requests; the feature is off by default, configurable at enterprise, organization, and repository levels, and an assessment alone does not satisfy merge requirements.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The selected approval and governance leaves track when AI-generated approval signals are admissible, which admin scope enabled them, and how they relate to merge rules and human review.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Review governance and MCP approval leaves for admin scope, default-off state, and merge-rule relationship.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub says enterprise-managed settings can set a preferred Copilot model as the default for new conversations, with team-specific defaults via managed JSON and team mappings across Copilot app, CLI, and VS Code for Business and Enterprise.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Partner selection and governance need evidence that model routing can be centrally owned, team-specific, and auditable across multiple agent clients instead of left to personal defaults.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Review partner-selection and governance leaves for team-scoped model-policy and override evidence.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub made Gemini 3.8 Flash available in Copilot and described early testing on complex terminal-based coding tasks with validation and persistent recovery from actionable failures; Business and Enterprise admins can manage access through model policy.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Selected eval, recovery, partner-selection, and governance leaves should treat model choice as a policy-gated workflow variable tied to validation and recovery evidence, not just model availability.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Review performance-gate and partner-selection leaves for model-policy, recovery, and validation evidence.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Curity argues that MCP OAuth authorization, MCP step-up authorization, and local tool-call control do not by themselves provide centralized, context-aware, organization-controlled authorization across agents; it proposes minimum, revocable task permissions mediated by a centralized policy/token-vaulting layer.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The selected MCP authorization and plugin-governance leaves need to distinguish protocol scopes, server-defined step-up controls, client-side tool confirmations, and centralized policy enforcement.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Review MCP approval and plugin packaging leaves for centralized policy versus per-server/per-client control boundaries.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: CData frames AI agent data governance around identity passthrough/RBAC, workspace isolation, SIEM-exportable audit trails, source-level data governance, OAuth/SAML passthrough, resource-bound permissions, token lifecycle management, and validating source access per environment.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The selected governance, readiness, MCP approval, and partner-selection leaves need infrastructure-level evidence for data access, audit, environment validation, token rotation, and least privilege before agents connect to enterprise data.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Review governance and environment-readiness leaves for source-access validation, identity passthrough, and SIEM evidence.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Express Computer/Gartner describes human checkpoint placement before execution, during execution, after execution, and through out-of-loop sampling, with triggers such as confidence thresholds, sensitive topics, constraint violations, value thresholds, and random sampling.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Selected lifecycle, hook, governance, and partner-selection leaves can use this as practice evidence for where a harness should pause, record, route, or sample agent work rather than treating human review as a single final gate.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Review lifecycle and hook leaves for checkpoint placement and trigger taxonomy.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: OpenAI Enterprise/Edu release notes add policy settings for browser and native app use on supported desktop clients, including website defaults/exceptions, upload/download/history/developer-access restrictions, automatic review, saved approvals, approval duration, and app allow/block rules. The same dated note adds Zendesk and OneNote plugins, where members connect their own accounts and admins manage availability separately.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Selected handoff, readiness, governance, plugin, and authorization leaves need evidence that cross-environment browser/native-app controls, saved approvals, plugin availability, and account-specific access are policy surfaces.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Review handoff, readiness, governance, and plugin leaves for browser/native-app controls and account-scoped plugin access.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Axios reports the proposed Stop Rogue AI Act would direct NIST to publish AI-agent deployment standards covering continuous maintenance and verification of agent actions, security/reliability evaluation, tamper-proof logs, and continuous machine-readable inventories of AI agents.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Governance and recovery leaves track the need for machine-readable agent inventories and tamper-proof action logs as infrastructure evidence for incident response and recurring agent operation.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Review governance and recovery leaves for inventory, tamper-proof logs, and action-verification evidence.
